title: Humayun And The Afghans
definition: The struggle between the early Mughal state under Humayun and the resurgent Afghan nobility, primarily led by Sher Shah Suri, representing the conflict between the nascent Mughal centralized authority and the traditional Afghan tribal confederacy.
importanceInUpsc: This period marks the critical 'interregnum' in Mughal history, testing the candidate's understanding of political instability, military strategy, and the transition from the Lodi-Afghan legacy to the Suri administration.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Humayun And The Afghans.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
